why: I checked each verifier check against the words of its expect line. Check 1 compares the output to "HELLO, ADA!", which is just the defined greeting `Hello, Ada!` in upper case, so it asks for nothing extra. Check 2 compares the output without the flag to the output from before the change, which is what "unchanged" means. Check 3 needs `--shout` in docs/index.md plus some explanation of it, which "documents" requires. Check 4 needs HTTP 200 and a line containing `--shout` on the published page, which is what "lists --shout" means. It also says a pre-merge FAIL depends on merge and deploy, which follows the line's "after merge". The stricter checks are all under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition)": npm test counts, the flag after the name, the usage line and exit code, and diff file scope. No PASS or FAIL condition demands more than its expect line's words.
